body: The on-scene phase of the investigation into the South Florida Learjet crash of November 1 has been completed, and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has handed over the scene. The Bombardier Learjet 60 crashed into the ground in Greenacres, Florida, killing all nine people on board. Federal investigators recovered the aircraft's cockpit voice recorder (CVR) from the wreckage, and it has been sent to the NTSB laboratory in Washington for readout and audio analysis.

Evidence found at the scene continues to point to a mid-air breakup. NTSB Board Member Tom Chapman confirmed that investigators found evidence the aircraft had begun to break up in the air before impact, with debris including a section of the tail located more than 3.8 miles (6.11 km) from the crater left by the high-speed impact. The jet encountered severe weather during its flight from Austin Bergstrom International Airport to the Bahamas: air traffic control audio recorded co-pilot Nathalia Filgueiras reporting icing conditions that caused severe turbulence above 700 feet (213 meters), before the crew issued a Mayday call. The loss of control and detachment of the tail control surfaces left the aircraft uncontrollable, and it entered a nose-down, high-speed descent into a residential roadway. The impact crater initially filled with water after heavy rain, which slowed parts of the recovery until the water was pumped out.

The investigation now moves to data extraction and laboratory analysis, including the download and evaluation of the voice recorder audio, mapping of the flight data and flight track against the severe convective storm cell on the flight path, and a structural examination of the airframe and tail assemblies to identify the sequence of the structural failure. A preliminary report is expected over the next few weeks, while the probable cause is not expected for up to two years. The aircraft was a Bombardier Learjet 60 registered N722BD, serial number 271, registered to LR60271 LLC and operated by charter company Aurora Aviation, powered by two Pratt & Whitney PW305A engines. All nine occupants were identified: Captain Jeff Gregory and co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20, and seven passengers — tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharep, their children Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, and the family nanny Anita Maria Cetina.
en.summary: The NTSB has recovered the cockpit voice recorder from the Learjet 60 that crashed in Greenacres, Florida, on November 1, killing all nine on board, and has ended the on-scene phase of the investigation as evidence continues to point to a mid-air breakup.
en.title: NTSB recovers cockpit voice recorder from Miami Learjet crash as on-scene investigation ends

body: 2026年11月1日南佛羅里達Learjet墜機事故的現場調查階段已經完成，美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）已將現場移交。這架龐巴迪Learjet 60墜毀於佛羅里達州格林埃克斯地面，機上9人全部罹難。聯邦調查人員已從殘骸中尋獲座艙語音紀錄器（CVR），並送往位於華盛頓的NTSB實驗室進行讀取與音訊分析。

現場發現的證據持續指向空中解體。NTSB委員Tom Chapman證實，調查人員發現證據顯示飛機在撞擊前已在空中開始解體，殘骸包括一段尾翼，位置距離高速撞擊形成的坑洞超過3.8英里（6.11公里）。這架飛機自奧斯汀伯格斯特龍國際機場飛往巴哈馬途中遭遇惡劣天氣：航管錄音記錄到副駕駛Nathalia Filgueiras回報結冰狀況造成700英尺（213公尺）以上嚴重亂流，隨後機組發出Mayday求救訊號。飛機失去控制且尾翼操縱面脫落後無法操控，隨即以機頭朝下高速俯衝，墜毀於一條住宅區道路。撞擊坑洞起初因豪雨積水，導致部分回收工作延誤，直到積水抽除後才恢復。

調查現已進入資料提取與實驗室分析階段，包括下載並評估語音紀錄器音訊、將飛行資料與航跡對照飛行路徑上的強對流風暴胞進行雷達與氣象重建，以及對機身與尾翼組件進行結構檢查，以確認結構失效的先後順序。初步報告預計於未來數週內發布，而可能肇因則可能需時長達兩年。涉事飛機為龐巴迪Learjet 60，註冊編號N722BD，序號271，登記於LR60271 LLC名下，由包機公司Aurora Aviation營運，配備兩具普惠PW305A發動機。9名罹難者身分均已確認：機長Jeff Gregory與副駕駛Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras（20歲），以及7名乘客——科技創業家Adam Robinson、其妻Helen Sharep、子女Emma（4歲）與Charlie（2歲）、家族友人Rachael Reed與Charmi Fehr，以及家庭保姆Anita Maria Cetina。
zh.summary: NTSB已尋獲11月1日墜毀於佛羅里達州格林埃克斯的Learjet 60座艙語音紀錄器，機上9人全部罹難，現場調查階段隨之結束，證據持續指向空中解體。
zh.title: NTSB尋獲邁阿密Learjet 60墜機座艙語音紀錄器現場調查階段結束
